rysen-works.title: RYSEN WORKS
rysen-works.summary: Internal staff can see which stage an order has reached, and handle delivery dates, inventory, and administrative approvals in the same system. The interface supports Chinese and Korean.
rysen-works.background: An order passes through purchasing, the warehouse, production, and shipment. Delivery dates, inventory, incoming materials, leave, and expenses are often kept in separate spreadsheets. Chinese- and Korean-speaking colleagues also have to confirm the same facts more than once. These records need to be viewed in one system.
rysen-works.solution: The workbench brings together upcoming delivery dates, milestones, and the stage of orders in progress. Orders are tracked as unfinished or finished, through order, purchasing, warehouse, production, shipment, and completion. The schedule places delivery dates, milestones, and leave on one calendar. Materials records stock and movements in and out. Administrative approvals cover leave, sick leave, explanations, expenses, and internal proposals.

rysen-works.audience: Purchasing, warehouse, production, and management staff who need to see order progress, delivery dates, inventory, and approvals together. After signing in, a customer sees only that customer’s own orders.
rysen-works.need: Staff need to know the current stage of an order, which delivery dates are coming due, whether stock is sufficient, and how far leave, expenses, and internal proposals have been approved.
rysen-works.approach: One web system covers the workbench, orders, schedule, materials, and administrative approvals. Orders move through six stages. Purchasing, warehouse, production, and customers each see a different scope. The interface can switch between Chinese and Korean.
rysen-works.effect: Opening the system shows orders as unfinished or finished, and the delivery dates that need attention now. Inventory changes and approvals stay in the same set of records.
rysen-works.value: Order progress, delivery dates, materials, and approvals sit in one system. Each role views and fills in what that role is responsible for. Chinese and Korean use the same interface. The English portfolio page shows the Chinese interface.
rysen-works.cta: Does your company also need orders, delivery dates, inventory, and approvals in one system? Ask about a setup that follows the way your team actually works.

cover.title: Workbench
cover.body: Brings together upcoming delivery dates, milestones, and the stage of orders in progress. Overdue items and items due today are marked separately.
cover.value: Purchasing, warehouse, and production can see today’s delivery dates and stages as soon as the system opens.

orders.title: Order stages
orders.body: Orders are split into unfinished and finished. The stages run from order, purchasing, warehouse, and production to shipment and completion.
orders.value: Opening an order shows how far it has progressed, and unfinished orders stay in one place.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.body: Delivery dates, sample milestones, and leave sit on one calendar as color blocks. Colors follow the order’s current stage, and overdue or near-due items are marked separately.
schedule.value: When planning a shipment, delivery dates and staff leave can be seen together.

inventory.title: Materials
inventory.body: Records material codes, specifications, shelf locations, and current quantities. When the warehouse changes a quantity, the inbound or outbound record and the reason remain. Purchasing and production can view them.
inventory.value: Stock changes stay in the system, so quantities do not have to be checked in a separate spreadsheet.

approvals.title: Administrative approvals
approvals.body: Covers leave, sick leave, explanations, expenses, and internal proposals. After a request is submitted, its status can be seen as pending, approved, or rejected.
approvals.value: Administrative items and business orders are submitted and followed in the same system.

files.title: Stage files and comments
files.body: Each stage can hold folders and attachments. Files uploaded by purchasing, warehouse, and production are reviewed by an administrator. People can leave comments in the stage, mention a colleague with {'@'}, and translate a comment into the other language.
files.value: Drawings, quotations, and discussion stay with the matching order and stage.

documents.title: PI, BOM, and shipment form
documents.body: A proforma invoice, purchasing BOM, and shipment form can be filled in from the order and exported to Excel after confirmation. The shipment form can record air or sea freight, the consignee, and how freight is paid.
documents.value: External documents are generated from the order, so the same content does not have to be copied into a spreadsheet.

arrivals.title: Incoming materials
arrivals.body: Records ordered quantity, delivered quantity, and the planned delivery date for each material, and separates not arrived, partially arrived, and fully arrived. An arrival can be linked to an order, and unlinked arrivals can still be viewed on their own.
arrivals.value: Purchasing and the warehouse can see which order still has materials outstanding.

customer.title: Customer view
customer.body: After signing in, a customer sees only that customer’s own orders and delivery dates. The schedule shows only the delivery dates and milestones for those orders, and it cannot be edited. Inventory, incoming materials, and internal approvals are not open to customers.
customer.value: Customers can check progress themselves, so internal staff handle fewer progress inquiries.

language.title: Chinese and Korean
language.body: The same interface can switch between Chinese and Korean. Order comments can be translated as well, so both sides read the same note.
language.value: Chinese-speaking and Korean-speaking colleagues work in the same system.

rysen-works.cardSummary: Orders, delivery dates, materials, and approvals sit in one system, with Chinese and Korean interfaces.

ssuker.audience: Business customers who need to present a forklift brand and its products
ssuker.need: Visitors need a quick view of the brand, the products, and specifications by tonnage.
ssuker.approach: The homepage opens with the brand hero. The specification area switches parameters by tonnage. The mobile first screen keeps the navigation, hero, and promotion.
ssuker.effect: Brand and product specifications can be read on both desktop and mobile.
ssuker.value: One corporate website presents the brand and product specifications in the order a visitor actually reads them.
ssuker.cta: Need a similar corporate website? Talk with RYSEN about a site shaped around your brand and products.

cover.title: Homepage brand hero

home.title: Specifications by tonnage
home.value: Customers can compare a specific model’s specifications.

mobile.title: Mobile first screen

massconnected.title: MASSCONNECTED
massconnected.summary: Visitors can tell what the platform does as soon as they open the site. After signing in and verifying email, buyers can post requests for CNC, sheet metal, injection molding, and other processes, start with an instant estimate, or use points to unlock a carton dieline. Verified factories quote online. Standard parts are purchased in the in-house shop. After a proposal is selected, contract confirmation, the payment voucher, and production progress stay in the same account. Process categories are maintained by operations and are not limited to these examples.
massconnected.background: Buyers need to post a manufacturing request by process, upload drawings, and compare quotes from verified factories. Some parts call for an estimate first, and cartons need a dieline. Standard parts need to be purchased directly. The contract, payment, and production progress should follow the same request.
massconnected.solution: The platform works as post a request, collect quotes, and compare before closing. Buyers can start with an instant estimate, unlock a carton dieline with points, and purchase standard parts in the in-house shop. The interface is available in Korean, Chinese, English, and Japanese, with Korean as the default.

captions.rfq: Post a request and compare quotes

massconnected.audience: Buyers who need factory quotes by process or want to purchase standard parts, and factories that quote and accept orders on the platform after verification
massconnected.need: Requests for quote, multiple proposals, instant estimates, carton dielines, and standard-part purchasing need to live on one platform. After a proposal is selected, contract confirmation, the payment voucher, and production progress should remain in the buyer account.
massconnected.approach: The platform works as post a request, collect quotes, and compare before closing. After signing in, a buyer posts a request or starts with an instant estimate. Verified factories quote in the demand hall. The buyer sees an organized proposal and does not see the factory identity. Standard parts go through the in-house shop. Cases, news, the FAQ, and the blog are updated by operations. The interface is available in Korean, Chinese, English, and Japanese, with Korean as the default.
massconnected.effect: Visitors can tell what the platform does as soon as they open the site. After signing in and verifying email, buyers can post requests for CNC, sheet metal, injection molding, and other processes, start with an instant estimate, or use points to unlock a carton dieline. Verified factories quote online. Standard parts are purchased in the in-house shop. After a proposal is selected, contract confirmation, the payment voucher, and production progress stay in the same account. Process categories are maintained by operations and are not limited to these examples.
massconnected.value: Quoting, comparison, standard-part purchasing, and the later contract, payment voucher, and production progress can all be handled on one platform. Browsing the site, cases, news, the blog, and products does not require an account. Posting a request, generating an instant estimate, and unlocking a dieline require sign-in and email verification. Shop checkout requires sign-in. Payment is a voucher uploaded by the buyer and confirmed by operations. The platform does not take online payment. Operations can review quotes, maintain processes and products, and update cases, news, and the blog.
massconnected.cta: Does your company need a similar manufacturing matchmaking platform? Talk with us about a site that fits your purchasing and quoting process.

cover.title: Understand the platform
cover.body: The homepage explains how buyers reach verified factories. Posting a request, collecting quotes, and comparing them before closing are also visible on that same screen.
cover.value: A visitor can see what the platform does, and which steps a request goes through.

homepage.title: How the platform works
homepage.body: The homepage puts posting a request, multiple quotes, and comparison before closing on one screen. Verified factories quote in the demand hall. The buyer sees an organized proposal and does not see the factory identity.
homepage.value: A visitor can see the quoting steps without leaving the page.

rfq.title: Post a request and compare quotes
rfq.body: Buyers enter quantity, material, and notes by process, and upload drawings. Verified factories claim the request in the demand hall and submit quotes. Buyers compare total price, unit price, tooling, samples, minimum order, lead time, and payment terms without seeing the factory identity.
rfq.value: One request is enough to compare several quotes and choose which proposal to continue.

estimate.title: Instant estimate
estimate.body: Injection molding, 3D printing, circuit boards, software, and chip design can produce an estimate from parameters and keep it on the account. For injection molding, buyers can also upload a 3D model or engineering drawing. The system suggests weight, slides, and material, and the buyer can revise the result before confirming.
estimate.value: Before a formal request, the buyer has an estimate that can be saved.

dieline.title: Carton dieline
dieline.body: Buyers choose a standard carton or a custom drawing and preview the dieline on the page. A standard carton can be adjusted by length, width, and height. A custom drawing stays at its original size. Points unlock the template for download, and downloading the same template again does not spend points.
dieline.value: Packaging design can take a dieline that matches the preview, without opening a quote first.

shop.title: Standard-parts shop
shop.body: Standard parts can be browsed by category, added to the cart, and checked out. The order stays on the buyer account. Browsing does not require sign-in. Checkout does.
shop.value: Parts that do not need custom manufacturing can be purchased on the same platform.

buyer.title: Buyer follow-up
buyer.body: The buyer workbench gathers items that need attention. The account center shows quotes, online contract confirmation, payment-voucher upload, production progress, and to-dos, plus points, notifications, and the NDA. Without email verification, a buyer cannot post a request, generate an instant estimate, or unlock a dieline. The buyer uploads a payment voucher, and operations confirm that it has arrived.
buyer.value: After a proposal is selected, the contract, payment, and production progress stay on the platform.

factory.title: Factory quoting and production
factory.body: A verified factory has its own workbench for quotes waiting, orders waiting to be accepted, and work in progress, plus a reference rate from renminbi to won. The factory can claim a public request, enter an itemized quote, accept or decline a production order, and update the production stage and progress. Buyers and factories can discuss the order on the platform.
factory.value: After signing in, the factory sees what needs attention, then moves into quoting or production.

blog.title: Content and languages
blog.body: Cases, news, the FAQ, downloads, and the blog are updated by operations. Blog posts can be found by category and keyword. Likes and comments require sign-in and email verification. Visitors cannot publish posts themselves. The interface is available in Korean, Chinese, English, and Japanese, with Korean as the default.
blog.value: Site explanations and process content can keep being updated, and each language uses the same business flow.

massconnected.cardSummary: Buyers post manufacturing needs by process, verified factories quote online, and standard parts can be purchased from the in-house shop.

odeokgu.title: 박순희와 오덕구
odeokgu.cardSummary: Buyers upload images and add text on the product page, then finish the acrylic light-stick customization with the product options.
odeokgu.summary: On the existing shop product, buyers place images and text, switch to the package-sticker area, and add the design to the cart after choosing cutting, handle printing, packaging, LED, and a quantity.
odeokgu.audience: Buyers who customize the artwork and text of an acrylic light stick on the product page
odeokgu.background: The shop already sells an acrylic light stick. Buyers need to arrange images and text, then choose cutting, handle printing, packaging, and LED before ordering.
odeokgu.need: Buyers need to design on the same product, see the dome and handle-print sizes, and continue to the cart with options and a quantity.
odeokgu.approach: The design area switches between the product and the package sticker. Buyers can upload an image, add text, use the asset library and layers, and adjust size and angle. Options appear in order: acrylic cutting, handle printing, packaging, and LED, with an option-cost total. Quantity has a limit, and larger quantities are directed to the Kakao channel.
odeokgu.effect: A finished design can be added to the cart and confirmed there. The page also explains where order details and Naver payment are handled.
odeokgu.value: Customization stays on the existing product. Buyers can confirm the artwork, text, package sticker, and options before ordering.
odeokgu.cta: Do you need shoppers to place artwork and text on an existing product? Ask about a customizer that fits the shop you already run.
odeokgu.solution: The design area sits on the existing light-stick product and switches between the product and the package sticker. Buyers upload images, add text, and use the asset library and layers to adjust size and angle. Options follow cutting, handle printing, packaging, and LED, and the finished design is confirmed in the cart.

cover.title: Light-stick design area
cover.body: The product is [커스텀] 아크릴 응원봉(입체형) - A TYPE. The design area switches between the product and the package sticker, with image upload, text, an asset library, and layers. The page shows the dome size and the handle-print size.
cover.value: Buyers start arranging the design on the product page.

text.title: Text and fonts
text.body: Buyers can add text, choose a font from the list, and adjust size and angle.
text.value: Wording and style are set before the item goes to the cart.

package.title: Package sticker
package.body: The design area can switch to the package sticker. A blue guide explains the printable area.
package.value: Package artwork is designed separately from the product artwork.

options.title: Options and quantity
options.body: Acrylic cutting, handle printing, packaging, and LED appear in that order, with an option-cost total. Quantity has a limit, and amounts above it are directed to the Kakao channel.
options.value: Buyers confirm the options before adding the item to the cart.

guide.title: Customization guide
guide.body: The guide covers image upload, text, the editing tools, and the package sticker.
guide.value: A first-time buyer can follow the steps on the same page.
